questions.text: A shareholder architect commits malpractice on a project. What source-backed responsibility statement applies to an architectural corporation?

options.text: RA 9266 makes no individual or collective responsibility possible.
Individual members are responsible for individual and collective acts as an entity and as provided by law.
Only non-architect shareholders are responsible.
The SEC replaces all professional responsibility.

questions.rationale: RA 9266 Section 37 provides the individual-and-collective responsibility language for registered firms, partnerships, associations, and corporations.

questions.text: An architectural corporation has one non-architect shareholder who wants to be chief executive officer. What RA 9266 composition rule must be checked?

options.text: Only shareholder percentage matters; executive officers are not mentioned.
RLAs must compose at least 75 percent of executive officers as applicable.
Any non-architect may hold all executive offices if SEC approves.
The rule applies only to sole proprietorships.

questions.rationale: Section 37 includes executive officers in the categories subject to the at-least-75-percent RLA composition rule.

questions.text: Which malpractice-insurance statement is source-safe from RA 9266 alone?

options.text: RA 9266 states corporate insurance always replaces individual responsibility.
RA 9266 supports professional responsibility; insurance placement needs a separate insurance or contract source.
RA 9266 forbids all insurance for corporations.
RA 9266 says only sole proprietors need insurance.

questions.rationale: The audited source supports registration, composition, and professional responsibility; insurance mechanics are not established in the cited excerpts.

questions.text: Which source-backed statement describes professional registration for an architectural corporation?

options.text: Only SEC registration is needed to practice architecture.
The Board may issue a certificate of registration to the corporation upon grant of registration, while individual professional qualifications still matter.
A non-architect corporation may practice architecture without RLAs.
DTI registration is the corporate route.

questions.rationale: RA 9266 Section 37 provides for Board/Commission registration of the entity, while emphasizing architecture as a professional service based on individual qualifications.

questions.text: An architectural corporation falls to 70 percent RLA composition because of share transfers. What must occur before it can be treated as compliant?

options.text: Nothing; compliance is checked only at incorporation.
The corporation must restore the at-least-75-percent RLA composition and, if non-compliant, comply and register again with SEC and BOA.
The 75 percent rule becomes 70 percent after registration.
The non-architect shareholders become RLAs automatically.

questions.rationale: The IRR states non-compliant existing architectural corporations must comply and register again with SEC and BOA; Section 37 sets the 75 percent floor.

questions.text: What happens when a proposed share transfer would reduce RLA composition below 75 percent?

options.text: The transfer is harmless under RA 9266.
The corporation cannot rely on that structure as RA 9266-compliant unless the 75 percent RLA composition is maintained or restored.
The corporation becomes a sole proprietorship.
BOA registration is no longer needed.

questions.rationale: Section 37 requires at least 75 percent RLA composition in the applicable categories.

questions.text: What regulatory registrations are source-backed for an architectural corporation?

options.text: DTI only
SEC registration and Board/PRC registration for architectural practice
Only an LGU business permit
No registration if the corporation has a design portfolio

questions.rationale: RA 9266 Section 37 requires SEC and Board registration; the UAP SPP frames group architectural practice through SEC/PRC registration.

questions.text: Can non-RLAs control the directors or executive officers of an architectural corporation?

options.text: Yes, if they provide capital.
No; RLAs must compose at least 75 percent of directors and executive officers, as applicable.
Yes, because Section 37 omits directors and officers.
Yes, if DTI registers the name.

questions.rationale: Section 37 expressly includes directors and executive officers in the 75 percent RLA composition rule.

questions.text: How should institutional continuity of an architectural corporation be treated in a source-safe RA 9266 answer?

options.text: RA 9266 alone supplies every corporate succession rule.
RA 9266 recognizes a registered entity, but corporate continuity mechanics need separate corporate-law or agreement support.
Continuity allows non-architects to ignore the 75 percent rule.
Continuity eliminates individual professional qualifications.

questions.rationale: RA 9266 supports entity registration and the RLA composition rule; detailed corporate continuity is outside the audited excerpts.

questions.text: What is the minimum RLA composition required by RA 9266 Section 37 for architectural corporations?

options.text: 25 percent
50 percent
At least 75 percent
No minimum once SEC registration exists

questions.rationale: Section 37 requires registered and licensed architects to compose at least 75 percent of the applicable categories.
